Name: Angie Fulton
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I learned that I am not teaching to my full potential and as a result I am not expecting the students best in return. I also need to remember that it is my job to teach scientific literacy and I have not been as intentional as I need to be with that. Teaching is so overwhelming and I get into survival mode and just do what I have done before. I need to do like you mentioned and pick a day of the week for writing as a starting point in all of my classes.

Share one artifact or anecdote from trying out your chosen strategy (e.g., a piece of student work, notes from your Writer’s Notebook, a classroom snapshot, or a brief story from the experience).:
What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

I need to merge these strategies with science content. I will allow some of our writing just to be for fun, but I also need to have students think deeper and make connections with science topics and concepts. This semester, I focused on one class doing writers notebooks, but I would like to implement them for all of my subjects next year.
